one-line facts about octopuses.
⏺ 1. Octopuses have three hearts.
2. Two hearts pump blood to the gills; one pumps it to the rest of the body.
3. Octopus blood is blue due to the copper-based protein hemocyanin.
4. They have eight arms, not tentacles.
5. Each arm has two rows of suckers.
6. The suckers can taste and smell what they touch.
7. Octopuses have no skeleton, allowing them to squeeze through tiny openings.
8. They are found in every ocean on Earth.

❯ Do not run any commands or use any tools. Write a numbered list of 60 short one-line facts about o
ctopuses.
⏺ 1. Octopuses have three hearts.
2. Two hearts pump blood to the gills; one pumps it to the rest of the body.
3. Octopus blood is blue due to the copper-based protein hemocyanin.
4. They have eight arms, not tentacles.
5. Each arm has two rows of suckers.
6. The suckers can taste and smell what they touch.
7. Octopuses have no skeleton, allowing them to squeeze through tiny openings.
8. They are found in every ocean on Earth.
9. Most octopus species live on the ocean floor.
10. The giant Pacific octopus is the largest species, reaching up to 14 feet across.
11. The smallest species, Octopus wolfi, is about an inch long.
12. Octopuses are cephalopod mollusks, related to squids and nautiluses.
13. They have a hard beak, similar to a parrot's, as their only rigid body part.
14. The beak is used to crack open crabs and clam shells.
15. Octopuses are highly intelligent invertebrates.
16. They can solve puzzles and open jars.
17. They have been observed using tools, such as carrying coconut shells for shelter.
18. Octopuses have excellent short- and long-term memory.
19. Their neurons are distributed throughout their arms, not just the brain.
20. About two-thirds of an octopus's neurons are in its arms.
21. Each arm can act semi-independently of the brain.
22. Octopuses can camouflage themselves in milliseconds.
23. They change color and texture using specialized skin cells called chromatophores.
24. They also have iridophores and papillae for additional texture and iridescence control.
25. Most octopuses are colorblind, yet they match colors with stunning accuracy.
26. One theory: they sense color through light-sensitive proteins in their skin.
27. When threatened, octopuses can release a cloud of ink to confuse predators.
28. The ink contains tyrosinase, which can irritate a predator's eyes and dull its sense of smell.
29. Octopuses can jet-propel themselves by expelling water through a siphon.
30. They can also walk along the seafloor on their arms.
31. Some species can briefly walk on land.
32. The mimic octopus impersonates other animals like flatfish, lionfish, and sea snakes.
33. Octopuses are generally solitary animals.
34. They are ambush predators, primarily eating crustaceans and fish.
35. They inject venom into prey to paralyze it.
36. All octopuses are venomous, but most pose no danger to humans.
37. The blue-ringed octopus is extremely dangerous — its venom can kill a human.
38. Blue-ringed octopuses flash bright rings as a warning display.
38. Blue-ringed octopuses flash bright rings as a warning display.
39. Octopuses have a lifespan of typically one to five years.
40. Most species die shortly after reproducing.
41. Males die weeks after mating.
42. Females die shortly after their eggs hatch, having stopped eating to guard the eggs.
43. A female octopus can lay up to 400,000 eggs.
44. She aerates and cleans the eggs constantly until they hatch.
45. Baby octopuses (paralarvae) are often planktonic when they first hatch.
46. Octopuses have a distributed immune system with no lymph nodes.
47. Their suckers can exert enormous gripping force relative to their size.
48. Octopuses can autotomize (voluntarily detach) an arm to escape a predator.
49. A detached arm can continue moving and responding for up to an hour.
50. Lost arms regenerate completely within a few weeks.
51. The dumbo octopus lives deeper than any other species — up to 13,000 feet down.
52. Dumbo octopuses get their name from ear-like fins on their heads.
53. Some octopuses build gardens of shells and debris outside their dens.
54. Octopuses have been observed throwing objects, including at other octopuses.
55. They show individual personalities — some are bold, others shy.
56. Octopuses can recognize individual human faces.
57. They have been observed playing with objects for apparent enjoyment.
58. The plural of octopus is "octopuses" — "octopi" is technically a Latinate error.
59. Octopuses have existed for at least 296 million years, predating the dinosaurs.
60. The word "octopus" comes from the Greek for "eight-footed."
